blocks.html: We continue to believe investors are increasingly drawn to ABF because of its contractual cash flows, collateral-backed structures, and ability to provide attractive income with limited dependence on corporate earnings growth or refinancing markets. Throughout the quarter, capital continued to migrate toward specialized asset-backed opportunities as banks remained selective; lenders and borrowers increasingly sought customized financing solutions backed by identifiable collateral pools. Against this backdrop, we remained focused on transactions featuring conservative advance rates, meaningful first-loss protection, dynamic borrowing bases, covenant protections, and strong servicing infrastructure. We believe these structural safeguards continue to distinguish many areas of ABF from broader corporate credit markets.

blocks.html: Looking ahead, we believe the environment remains favorable for experienced ABF investors despite continued macroeconomic uncertainty. Markets are navigating a period of evolving Federal Reserve policy, elevated geopolitical risks, and ongoing debate regarding the timing and magnitude of future interest rate adjustments. While these factors may contribute to periodic volatility, they have generally increased dispersion across sectors rather than creating broad-based credit stress. In our view, this environment continues to reward disciplined underwriting, careful asset selection, and a focus on structural protections.

blocks.html: We remain constructive on the long-term outlook for ABF. Continued bank retrenchment, growth in non- bank lending, expanding capital needs across consumers and businesses, and increasing institutional adoption of asset-backed financing solutions continue to support a broad and growing opportunity set. At the same time, tighter public market spreads and elevated investor demand have reinforced the importance of maintaining valuation and underwriting discipline. We continue to favor opportunities offering strong collateral coverage, conservative leverage, and clear downside mitigation potential5, while selectively rotating capital toward areas where we believe risk-adjusted returns remain most compelling.

blocks.html: We deployed capital across a diverse set of asset-based opportunities spanning technology-enabled business services and consumer finance during the quarter. New investments included a first-lien growth financing for a scaled corporate travel and spend management platform, a mezzanine warehouse backed by predominantly prime medical point-of-sale loans, and an investment in an asset fund financing short- duration consumer receivables across multiple emerging markets. While the underlying assets and business models differ, each transaction reflects our emphasis on identifiable sources of repayment, meaningful asset coverage and structural protections, including first-lien collateral, excess spread, overcollateralization, dynamic advance rates and performance triggers. Collectively, these investments broaden portfolio diversification while preserving our focus on downside protection and attractive risk- adjusted returns.

blocks.html: Looking forward, we remain constructive on the asset-based finance opportunity set, while continued macroeconomic and policy uncertainty reinforces the importance of selectivity and a high-quality bias. We continue to manage the portfolio through a disciplined relative-value framework, rotating across sectors and structures based on risk-adjusted return potential and available downside protection. Within consumer and small business credit, we remain selective and favor short-duration, structurally protected exposures, while continuing to broaden the portfolio across receivables lending, hard assets and other differentiated collateral types where relative value is compelling. Across the portfolio, our emphasis remains on conservative attachment points, strong covenant packages and rigorous downside stress testing. Overall, we believe the current environment favors patience and active portfolio rotation while continuing to deploy capital selectively into opportunities with attractive structural protections.

Deal Merits:

items: Strong growth and retention profile, supported by recurring customer activity, attractive gross margins, and an established European market position.
Differentiated platform with broad travel inventory and automation capabilities that support customer stickiness and operating efficiency.
First-lien structure with meaningful lender protections, including leverage, revenue growth and minimum-liquidity covenants, together with significant equity value beneath the debt.

blocks.text: Key Considerations:

items: Corporate travel cyclicality: Revenue depends on travel commissions, booking fees and transaction volumes, which tend to fall when the economy weakens or corporate travel budgets are cut. SMB customers (70-80% of base) have inelastic travel demand — Amazon warehouse crews, solar panel installers, Liverpool City Council — they must travel to do their jobs. Furthermore, the company does not buy travel inventory in advance and operates in an agency capacity, so in a demand collapse (e.g., COVID) it did not incur inventory losses / liabilities to travel providers

Growth-stage profile and North American expansion risk: The company is still investing heavily in geographic expansion and technology, and the North American growth plan has execution risk. This is mitigated by its established European position, attractive gross margins and growing operating leverage, plus a leverage covenant and significant equity value beneath the debt.

Competitive landscape: The travel and spend management market is competitive, and established and new players are investing in similar features. The company’s broad travel inventory, automation capabilities and integrated booking-and-spend offering support customer stickiness.

Deal Merits:

items: High-quality collateral pool characterized by predominantly prime borrowers, required upfront payments and historically consistent credit performance.
Significant asset coverage from excess spread and hard credit enhancement, with underwriting indicating approximately 1.9x breakeven coverage relative to the base loss case.
Robust structural protections, including dynamic LTV adjustments, eligibility criteria, concentration limits and collateral and managed-pool performance triggers.

blocks.text: Key Considerations:

items: Mezzanine position in the capital structure: NBSF’s position covers roughly the 80%–95% LTV slice of the collateral, so it would absorb losses before the senior lender if collateral performance weakens badly. This is mitigated by the excess spread and hard credit enhancement below NBSF’s position, about 1.9x breakeven coverage against the base loss case, and dynamic LTV adjustments.

Consumer credit and discretionary spending exposure: The loans finance elective procedures such as dental, medical spa and cosmetic work. Demand and borrower repayment could weaken in a consumer downturn. Mitigants are the predominantly prime borrowers with high average credit scores and strong incomes, required upfront payments and high autopay enrollment.

Merchant and originator dependence: Collateral quality depends on the platform’s ongoing underwriting discipline and the health of its merchant network. Eligibility criteria, concentration limits, collateral and managed-pool performance triggers, and the platform’s access to diversified warehouse and securitization funding all help offset this.

Deal Merits:

items: Attractive unlevered return supported by high-yielding underlying assets, substantial excess spread and short-duration receivables.
Meaningful asset coverage, with a 105% minimum overcollateralization requirement and typical advance rates meaningfully below the contractual maximum.

Strong alignment through a structure in which the manager charges no servicing, management or performance fees and its economics are subordinated behind the warehouse interest passed through to fund investors.

blocks.text: Key Considerations:

items: Emerging-market exposure: The fund lends across nine geographies, mostly in Latin America. That brings macroeconomic, regulatory and political risks that don’t arise in developed-market consumer lending. The short duration of the receivables limits how long the fund is exposed, and spreading lending across multiple jurisdictions reduces reliance on any one market.

Subprime and underbanked consumer credit risk: The borrowers carry higher credit risk than developed-market prime consumers. High asset yields, substantial excess spread, the 105% minimum overcollateralization requirement and advance rates typically well below the contractual maximum all help absorb losses.

Reliance on local operating subsidiaries: The fund’s collateral and repayment come from loans to local operating subsidiaries, so operational, servicing and legal-enforcement risk differs by jurisdiction. This is mitigated by the senior secured structure at the asset level, consistent asset performance since NBSF’s relationship began in 2022, and alignment from the manager subordinating its own economics behind payments to fund investors.

blocks.html: Opportunity: NBSF formed a strategic aircraft leasing partnership with the operating partner and acquired an initial portfolio of mid-life Boeing 737 and Airbus A320 aircraft. items: Attractive contracted cash flows supported by hard assets, with aircraft leases providing current income and residual value supported by a global secondary market for commercial aircraft.
Diversified portfolio of highly utilized aircraft types, focused on widely flown Boeing 737 and Airbus A320 narrowbody families that can be repositioned across airlines and geographies.

Partnership with a scaled global aircraft operator provides sourcing, underwriting, servicing, remarketing and repossession capabilities, while NBSF retains control over major investment, financing and disposition decisions.
Favorable aviation supply-demand dynamics, with constrained aircraft production and supply- chain bottlenecks supporting demand for the existing fleet.

blocks.text: Key Considerations:

items: Lessee credit and repossession risk: Lease cash flows depend on airline credit, and airlines are vulnerable to economic shocks, fuel prices and geopolitical events. The portfolio is spread across multiple airlines and geographies, and the operating partner has repossession and remarketing capabilities if an airline defaults.
Residual value and re-leasing risk: Returns on the mid-life aircraft partly depend on what they can be re-leased or sold for when their leases expire. This is mitigated by the focus on widely

Neuberger’s business activities as well as the activities of the Fund and its operations and investments could be materially adversely affected by global outbreaks of disease, epidemics and public health issues. In particular, coronavirus, or COVID-19, spread rapidly around the world since its initial emergence in December 2019 and negatively affected the global economy, global equity markets and supply chains. Although the long-term effects of coronavirus, or COVID-19 cannot be completely predicted, previous occurrences of other epidemics, pandemics and outbreaks of disease, had material adverse effects on the economies, equity markets and operations of those countries and jurisdictions in which they were most prevalent. A recurrence of an outbreak of any kind of epidemic, communicable disease, virus or major public health issue could cause a slowdown in the levels of economic activity generally (or push the world or local economies into recession), which is likely to adversely affect the business, financial condition and operations of Neuberger and the Fund. Should these or other major public health issues, including pandemics, arise or spread farther (or continue to worsen), Neuberger and the Fund could be adversely affected by more stringent travel restrictions, mandatory quarantines and social distancing and additional limitations on Neuberger’s (or the Fund’s) operations and business activities.

Further, governmental actions (sanctions-related, military or otherwise) may cause additional disruption and constrain or alter existing financial, legal and regulatory frameworks and systems in ways that are adverse to the investment strategy that the Fund intends to pursue, all of which could adversely affect the Fund’s ability to fulfill its investment objectives. Additionally, to the extent that third parties, investors, or related customer bases have material operations or assets in any of the impacted countries, they may have adverse consequences related to the ongoing conflict.
